links.comparator_used: Not clearly stated in the abstract; the SHAP bar chart of acoustic feature influence was evaluated across eight factors in two user studies, with no explicit no-attribution arm described.
links.outcome: Clinician-student interpretation of SHAP feature attributions for AI dysarthria detection (understandability, decision relevance, mental model, trust, cognitive load, task performance)
links.effect: No numeric effects in the abstract. The bar chart frequently misled participants into reading feature influence as clinical severity. Participants had difficulty understanding AI mechanisms, saw discrepancies between human and model reasoning, and the chart had limited ability to address clinical questions.
links.tradeoff: New failure mode: feature influence misread as clinical severity. The authors also note the interpretations may add burden and bias, because acoustic features are unfamiliar to clinicians and misaligned with workflows.
links.quote: The seemingly intuitive bar-chart design frequently misled participating speech-language pathology (SLP) students to interpret feature influence as an indicator of clinical severity.
